models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Thirteen days out: current pattern is light NW and near-flat seas, but nothing yet covers our trip dates.
briefing.synopsis: Through 22 Sep the Aeolians sit under a slack, weakly gradient pattern with winds predominantly from the NW backing W at times, generally 2-7 kt across Portorosa, Lipari, Salina, Panarea, Filicudi and Stromboli (ECMWF IFS 0.25 / AIFS, 19 Sep 18Z; ICON-2i, 19 Sep 12Z). Gusts are mostly 6-15 kt, with isolated IFS maxima of 17-20 kt at Panarea and Stromboli overnight 19/20 Sep - note IFS gusts are interval maxima, so they look large in light air. Seas are near-flat: total wave 0.06-0.36 m and swell 0.04-0.34 m (MFWAM and ECMWF WAM, 19 Sep 12Z/18Z), with a slow rebuild toward 0.30-0.36 m around Stromboli, Panarea and Filicudi late on 22 Sep. If this regime held it would mean motor-sailing conditions and comfortable anchorages, but the forecast only reaches 26 Sep - it says nothing about 3 Oct.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: No berth or mooring data is included in this payload, so I cannot recommend a specific anchorage tonight. What the data does show is that swell everywhere in the group currently runs 0.04-0.34 m, which is below any threshold that would force a move. Berth-by-berth guidance will come once the itinerary legs enter the forecast window, roughly a week from departure.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: For the current period, mornings are the lightest part of the day: 21 Sep 06:00 shows 1.9-5.1 kt NW across the islands with waves 0.12-0.14 m (ECMWF IFS 0.25, 19 Sep 18Z). Departure windows for our own legs cannot be assessed yet - the model horizon ends 26 Sep 23:00, a week before we sail. Expect the first meaningful look at day-one timing around 27-28 Sep, and a firm one three to four days out.

passage_notes.note: No leg forecasts in this payload - every planned passage sits beyond the 26 Sep model horizon. Nothing to plan around yet.

cautions: Nothing in the current data is of concern: winds 2-7 kt, seas under 0.4 m. This is a benign pattern, not a forecast for our trip.

Where models diverge they diverge widely in light air: Lipari 22 Sep midday 5.8-13.3 kt, Panarea 22 Sep evening 2.3-10.1 kt, Stromboli 22 Sep evening 1.7-8.4 kt (ECMWF IFS/AIFS vs ICON-2i). Treat the consensus figures as indicative only.
ICON-2i runs only ~60-72 h and drops out of any longer-range view; AIFS publishes no gust field, so all gust numbers come from IFS and ICON-2i.
briefing.confidence_note: The models agree well on the benign pattern through 22 Sep, but the trip dates are 13 days out and entirely beyond the 26 Sep forecast horizon, so there is no skill for our actual sailing window.
